questions.prompt: How many camera setups and main actions should one shot prompt hold?

options.text: One camera setup and one subject action.
options.explanation: Both guides say one clear idea per shot. Packing several shots into one leaves the model to guess the framing and order.

options.text: As many as fit, to save requests.
options.explanation: A prompt that packs several shots into one clip tends to blur them.

options.text: None. Video models decide the camera on their own.
options.explanation: Camera positioning and motion are prompt elements in Google's guide.

questions.prompt: A character must speak a line in a Veo video. How does Google's guide say to write the speech?

options.text: Put the exact words in quotes.
options.explanation: Right. The guide says: use quotes for specific speech.

options.text: Describe only the topic, not the words.
options.explanation: Then the model chooses the words.
Google's guide lists dialogue, sound effects and ambient noise as audio cues.

questions.prompt: What does Veo do with an image you give it as the input to start a video?

options.text: It uses the image as the first frame.
options.explanation: Right. Google's docs say Veo uses the input image as the initial frame.

options.text: It uses the image as the last frame.
options.explanation: A last frame is a separate option. A plain input image is the start.

options.text: It ignores the image and uses only the text.
options.explanation: The image is the starting scene.
